subject: monsterTruck
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: monster truck with huge tyres.
Style: pixel art.
reasoning:
I'm deciding to build this as a static model using the pixel kit imports, planning a monster truck with realistic proportions—roughly 1.7m diameter tires scaled to real monster truck sizing—and figuring out body length from there.

Now I'm sketching out the full parts list: tread-textured tires with hub caps and lug nuts, axles with coil-rod shocks, dual chassis rails with crossmembers, and a tileBox body including cab, hood, textured windows, grille, glowing headlights, bumper, roll bar, exhaust stacks, flame decals, number plate, wheel arches, and a spoiler.

Working out tread block rotation around the tire's axis...

Now I'm laying out the tyre positions and track width versus a narrower body, then working through the chassis rails, floor, lower tub, cab, and hood dimensions and heights to stack them properly on the frame.

I'm adding the hood detail, windshield and side window planes facing outward from the cab, a rear window and roof box, a front grille plane sized to the tub's front face, glowing headlight boxes, a front bumper, and mirrored flame texture planes on each side of the tub.

The flame orientation on each side is tricky since the plane normals and texture directions could mirror unpredictably, so I decide to skip adding text to the flames and just keep them symmetric-looking. I also check whether the tub overlaps the tyres given their coordinate ranges, confirming the tub's z-span relative to the tyres' height and position.

Since the tub sits too low and clips into the tyres, I raise it above the tyre top to expose the chassis between, giving it that classic monster truck look. I then rework the dimensions: a taller tub positioned higher, a cab sitting above and behind it, plus a small hood scoop box on top, bringing the total vehicle height to around 3.4 units.

Now I'm adding the rear bed section behind the cab, a roll bar, and a spoiler, then building the suspension system with diagonal four-link rods and shock absorbers running from the axles up to the tub using simple rod and ring-box shapes. I still need the axle boxes, driveshaft, differential, and hub caps, all built using the box() helper function.

For the surface details, I'm setting up pixel textures: a gradient window texture with highlight diagonals, a barred grille pattern, and a flame decal generated by a height function that creates rising orange and yellow flame shapes along the front of the body.

For the wheels, I'm cell-painting the tires with randomized grey ramps for a rubber texture, using a 16-segment cylinder, then adding gold hub discs with lug nut boxes and a lighter sidewall ring for detail.

Beyond the wheels, I'm placing twin steel exhaust stacks behind the cab, plus glowing headlight and taillight boxes and a roof-mounted light bar across the cab's front.
